# What's new in the world of Search

Day 1, 11:35 · Gary Illyes, Search Relations · coverage: transcript, slides

Speaker from his self-introduction at the start of the talk, in a second attendee recording.

## Claims

- **[Slide]** AI Mode queries have doubled every quarter since launch.
  <br><sub>`D1-C016` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D1-C184](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** The average AI Mode query is about 3 times the length of a traditional search (the opening keynote's slide and its speaker said two to three times).
  <br><sub>`D1-C017` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *AI Mode*</sub>

- **[Slide]** One in six AI Mode searches is multimodal, using voice or images.
  <br><sub>`D1-C018` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D3-C562](D3-S16-mastering-the-messy-middle.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Follow-up queries in AI Mode have grown by more than 40% per month on average in the US since launch.
  <br><sub>`D1-C019` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *AI Mode*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google describes four new ways people search in AI Mode: Explore (brainstorming queries, grown 30% faster than AI Mode queries overall in the US since launch), Learn (study guides, deep dives), Decide (searches beginning with 'which', up 40% faster than AI Mode queries overall in the past six months) and Do (planning queries, up 80% faster than AI Mode queries overall in the past six months).
  <br><sub>`D1-C020` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Queries of five or more words are growing in volume 1.5 times faster than shorter queries. The slide footnote cites Google internal data on global English-language queries, for a comparison period that starts in November 2022 (the remaining dates are only partly legible).
  <br><sub>`D1-C021` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D1-C185](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Search Agents in AI Mode let users set standing requests for updates, such as being told when a product goes on sale, a team wins or a price drops below a level.
  <br><sub>`D1-C022` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D1-C192](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Extended by [D1-C194](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google listed eight ways AI Search helps users find and visit websites: preferred sources expansion, fresh perspectives and prominent links, subscription content, in-line quotes in AI Mode and AI Overviews, rich linking and embedded web, context on content sources, 'Highly Cited' labels and Search profiles.
  <br><sub>`D1-C023` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Users can link their subscriptions so answers highlight paywalled content they already pay for; The Indian Express saw 34% more engagement among linked subscribers.
  <br><sub>`D1-C024` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Publishers and creators can claim a dedicated Search profile with a name, profile photo, cover image, bio, connected social and website accounts, pinned posts and links, and users can follow it.
  <br><sub>`D1-C025` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [A new profile to help publishers and creators highlight their work on Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/a-new-profile-to-help-publishers-and-creators-highlight-their-work-on-search/), [Manage your Search profile](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/16904750?hl=en) · Extended by [D3-C468](D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Used by the glossary term *Search profile*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Search profiles launched on 4 June 2026, in the US first, for creators and publishers with a sizable following on at least one major social or video platform. They appear in knowledge panels and Discover.
  <br><sub>`D1-C026` · Google blog (4 June 2026) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [A new profile to help publishers and creators highlight their work on Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/a-new-profile-to-help-publishers-and-creators-highlight-their-work-on-search/) · Updated by [D1-C125](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Since 16 September 2026, US publishers and creators qualify for a Search profile with 10,000 followers across YouTube, Instagram, X or TikTok, and media organisations can claim and manage profiles for all their sub-brands from one login.
  > "We've lowered the eligibility threshold to 10,000 followers across YouTube, Instagram, X, or TikTok."
  <br><sub>`D1-C125` · Google blog (16 September 2026) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [3 new ways we're improving Search profiles for publishers](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/3-new-ways-were-improving-search-profiles-for-publishers/) · Updates [D1-C026](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Used by the glossary term *Search profile*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Sites that users mark as a preferred source are more visible in Top Stories and are labelled in AI Mode and AI Overviews.
  <br><sub>`D1-C027` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D3-C317](D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Preferred sources, linked subscriptions and Search profiles all depend on users acting on a brand's behalf. They reward brands with a loyal audience and do little for anonymous lead-generation sites.
  <br><sub>`D1-C028` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search</sub>

- **[Slide]** Search Console has a property setting called Search generative AI that gives direct control over AI Overviews and AI Mode without affecting web rankings. Its states are inherit from parent, include and exclude.
  > "Direct control over AI Overviews and AI Mode without impacting web rankings."
  <br><sub>`D1-C029` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Extended by [D2-C103](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Repeated by [D3-C436](D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-10`, `F-012`, the glossary term *Search generative AI control*</sub>

- **[Docs]** The Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover. Excluding removes both links to the site and use of its content to ground answers.
  <br><sub>`D1-C030` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Repeated by [D2-C103](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-10`, the glossary term *Search generative AI control*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google says the control is not used as a ranking or inclusion signal for regular results.
  > "this control isn't used as a ranking or inclusion signal"
  <br><sub>`D1-C031` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-IDX-10`, `F-012`, the glossary term *Search generative AI control*</sub>

- **[Docs]** The control does not affect AI training. Training of the models is limited with Google-Extended instead.
  <br><sub>`D1-C032` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-IDX-11`, the glossary term *Google-Extended*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Changes to the control generally apply within 1–2 days, though some content takes longer. It works at property level only, and a child property inherits from its closest parent that changed the setting.
  <br><sub>`D1-C033` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-IDX-10`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Lead-generation, local-service and e-commerce sites should normally stay included, because AI answers cite and link sources. Sites selling paywalled or licensed content should test exclusion on a child property first. Use nosnippet only if you also want out of regular snippets.
  <br><sub>`D1-C034` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · Extended by [D2-C072](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-10`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Knowing how Search works largely means knowing how the AI features work.
  > "If you know how Search works, you largely also know how AI features work."
  <br><sub>`D1-C035` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes argued that GEO is a label invented to create a new field and is not needed. Understanding how SEO works is enough.
  <br><sub>`D1-C049` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Contradicted by [D1-C296](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) · Used by `A-001`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said that in about 30 years of web search, helping users complete their journeys has made them search more, not less, unlike a product whose problem is solved once and for all.
  <br><sub>`D1-C182` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · Extends [D1-C001](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said Gen Z users are a very large part of Google Search's user base and search differently from older users, for example with images.
  <br><sub>`D1-C183` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said AI Mode is growing almost exponentially and that people are searching more because of it, not less.
  <br><sub>`D1-C184` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [A new era for AI Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/) · Extends [D1-C016](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Extends [D1-C004](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said a multi-part query, such as a white three-row SUV for two teenagers and a car-sick dog, cannot be satisfied by a list of links because no single article covers every aspect, while AI Overviews and AI Mode can synthesise an answer that helps users decide where to go.
  <br><sub>`D1-C185` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Extends [D1-C021](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said that in the mid-1990s searchers had to speak machine, typing queries like 'weather Barcelona rain', whereas today machines understand how people naturally speak.
  <br><sub>`D1-C186` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google presented the intelligent search box as one of its recent Search launches; it accepts long queries and keeps expanding to make room for them.
  <br><sub>`D1-C187` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · confirmed by Google docs · [A new era for AI Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/) · Extends [D1-C150](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said it noticed young users uploading pictures to reverse image search and expecting results that answer something about the picture, and that Google Lens was its answer to that behaviour.
  <br><sub>`D1-C188` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *Google Lens*</sub>

- **[Stage]** AI Overviews and AI Mode work together: a user can start with an AI Overview and continue the conversation in AI Mode.
  <br><sub>`D1-C189` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · confirmed by Google docs · [A new era for AI Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/) · Extends [D1-C152](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said Google Lens is used by over 1.5 billion people (figure as said on stage on 30 September 2026; no period was given).
  <br><sub>`D1-C190` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · confirmed by Google docs · [AI in Search: Going beyond information to intelligence](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-search-ai-mode-update/)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's May 2025 Search announcement says more than 1.5 billion people use Google Lens to search what they see every month.
  > "Google Lens, which more than 1.5 billion people are using to search what they see every month"
  <br><sub>`D1-C191` · Google blog (20 May 2025) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [AI in Search: Going beyond information to intelligence](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-search-ai-mode-update/) · Used by the glossary term *Google Lens*</sub>

- **[Press]** A search marketing agency reported on 29 September 2026 that Google's VP of Product for Search announced on X, on 28 September 2026, that AI Mode information monitoring was rolling out to everyone globally in the Google app; Google's I/O 2026 post had launched information agents first for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in summer 2026.
  <br><sub>`D1-C193` · Relevant Audience (29 September 2026), Google blog (19 May 2026) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the press report · [Google rolls out AI Mode info monitoring to everyone globally](https://www.relevantaudience.com/seo/google-ai-mode-info-monitoring-global-rollout/), [A new era for AI Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A Search agent is set up by typing a natural-language request, which AI Mode interprets to create an alert; Google called this an information agent.
  <br><sub>`D1-C194` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [A new era for AI Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/) · Extends [D1-C022](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Used by the glossary term *Search agents (information agents)*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said it would roll out agentic capabilities that allow bookings later in 2026, in the US only at first.
  <br><sub>`D1-C195` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [A new era for AI Search](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said Search Console's generative AI reporting launched alongside the generative AI control, starting with impressions only, and may expand later.
  <br><sub>`D1-C196` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports), [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Repeats [D1-C124](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Repeated by [D3-C440](D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes traced 'SEO is dead' predictions back to a post titled 'Search engine R.I.P.' on an online advertising forum on 10 November 1997, and said such posts still appear every month or even every week.
  <br><sub>`D1-C197` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · Used by `A-001`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said SEO is not dead and that the new AI features only create more opportunities for site owners to take advantage of.
  <br><sub>`D1-C198` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · Extends [D1-C050](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Used by `A-001`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes said searching by image or by video, as Search offers it today, was not possible before transformers were invented.
  <br><sub>`D1-C199` · Day 1, What's new in the world of Search (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C161](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Visual search predates transformers in Google's own history: its Search timeline dates Google Images to 2001 and Google Lens to 2017, the year Google Research published the Transformer, so read the stage remark as being about today's multimodal AI search.
